Subject: Scheduling: pricing & security run-through + usage forecast

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time on Friday. As discussed, we'd like to schedule a single, cross-functional session to cover:
- high-level demo (AE + SE, 20–25 min)
- usage forecast walk-through (15 min)
- dedicated capacity & pricing conversation (15–20 min)
- security / compliance Q&A (as time allows)

Goal: get procurement and InfoSec comfortable with the operational model and align on sizing/forecast so we can move to a committed capacity recommendation.

Proposed slots (PDT):
• Tue Apr 5, 09:00–10:00
• Tue Apr 5, 13:00–14:00
• Wed Apr 6, 10:00–11:00

I've attached a one-page usage forecast template and a short pricing summary to speed the prep. Can you confirm who from Eng should join, and whether procurement/security should be looped in? If those times don't work, send a few alternatives and we’ll re-sync.

Attachments: RW_Usage_Forecast_Template.xlsx; RW_Dedicated_Pricing_Summary.pdf

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

jasmine.liu@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Hi all —

Confirming SE availability for Tue Apr 5, 13:00–14:00 PDT. Proposed agenda from the SE side:
- 10 min: walk through request patterns & latency SLOs (what we saw in your initial telemetry)
- 20 min: dedicated sizing recommendation (GPU type, queue depth, estimated concurrency) + cost per 1M tokens with/without KV cache
- 10 min: integration considerations (prefix caching, batching)

I’ll bring the quick security notes that map to the Security_QA_Summary.pdf (attached). If Tom wants a deeper dive, we can schedule a follow-up with our infra security lead.

Thanks — putting procurement expectations on the table so the session is productive:
- we need an outline of the contractual cadence (PO → pilot → committed capacity) and any minimum term/notice windows
- a short SLA summary (availability targets, credits)
- data handling & residency commitments (we are reviewing EU residency for some workloads)
- high-level pricing bands and a worked example using the forecast template

I’ve attached our internal procurement checklist to make sure nothing is missed on our side (BrightWave_Procurement_Checklist.docx).

If you can either (a) call out the contractual bullets in the agenda or (b) follow with a one-page summary post-meeting, that will speed procurement review.

Sara Lin
Senior Procurement Manager, BrightWave
sara.lin@brightwave.com

Team — thanks for the quick responses. Finalizing per the thread:
- Confirmed: Tue Apr 5, 13:00–14:00 PDT (calendar invite sent)
- Attendees: Alex Morgan (BrightWave Eng), Tom Reynolds (BrightWave InfoSec), Sara Lin (Procurement), Jasmine Liu (AE), Dev Patel (SE), Rishi Malhotra (solutions - pricing), Laura Bennett (Sales Ops)
- Agenda (60 min): 1) 20-min demo + dataflow overview (AE/SE) 2) 20-min sizing & pricing worked example (SE/Rishi) 3) 15-min procurement & contractual items (AE + Procurement) 4) 5-min next steps and action items

Pre-reads (please review before the call): RW_Usage_Forecast_Template.xlsx; RW_Dedicated_Pricing_Summary.pdf; Security_QA_Summary.pdf. I’ve also dropped a shared folder with a one-page contractual summary and the forecast I’d like BrightWave to populate: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEF_shared_runbook

Notes on outcomes we’ll aim for:
- Aligned committed capacity recommendation (target: a single recommended configuration and a range of expected monthly token throughput)
- Procurement checklist acceptance or list of open items
- An owner for any follow-ups (Rishi will own worked pricing examples; Dev will own technical follow-ups; Jasmine will own commercial/contractual items)

Calendar invite includes the shared doc and a Calendly backup link if we need to move: https://calendly.com/jasmine-liu/rw-pricing-call

Thanks — see you Tue.

Best,
